title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Auditorium on 1967-11-11
lineage: MSR > R > R > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture with crisp early set and standout performances of Schoolgirl, Lovelight, Death Don't Have No Mercy and New Potato Caboose, despite a bit of muddiness on the later tracks.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid soundboard source that delivers clear, punchy audio for most of the show, though tracks 4‑7 get a little muddy. Musically the band is on fire – Pigpen’s organ solo, Jerry’s soaring lead on Lovelight, and scorching renditions of Schoolgirl, Death Don't Have No Mercy and New Potato Caboose make this 1967 gem a must‑hear.

ai_rating.rationale: Across 16 reviews the average rating is >4, with consistent praise for both performance and sound quality; only minor complaints about occasional muddiness.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and clear soundboard recording; some reviewers note midside muddiness on tracks 4‑7 and a touch of funkiness at the start of Lovelight, but overall very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong early set with tight transitions; the show maintains high energy throughout, even though a few songs (e.g., Born Cross‑Eyed) were not yet in rotation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Lead guitar solo on Lovelight praised; overall described as 'on fire' and delivering tight, fiery playing.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen's organ work highlighted – an impressive solo and solid keyboard presence throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s glockenspiel contribution on New Potato Caboose noted; drums provide a steady, energetic foundation.
